<Subject 1> is the SAME ADULT woman game character shown in <Picture 1>. <Picture 1> is the authoritative identity, face, hair, costume, accessory and footwear reference. Reproduce her specific design faithfully in every view; do not invent a new character. Transfer ONLY the woman and her design, never the outdoor trees, lanterns, ribbons, leaves, path or scenery.

TASK AND LAYOUT
Create ONE finished professional 3D Character Design Reference Sheet, a static 16:9 landscape studio presentation board. The large turnaround zone is visibly WIDER than the close-up grid: allocate 60% width to the three full-body views and ONLY 40% width to the close-up grid. The entire background is seamless pure white. The LEFT 60 percent of the board contains EXACTLY THREE equally sized FULL-BODY turnaround renders, arranged horizontally: FRONT, strict 90-degree SIDE, strict 180-degree BACK, in that order. The RIGHT 40 percent contains EXACTLY TWELVE detail close-ups in a precise THREE-COLUMN, FOUR-ROW rectangular grid. Every detail cell has identical width and height and a very thin straight black border. This is a single board with 3 full-body views plus 12 detail panels, not a repeating full-body grid, not an animation sequence. NO written titles, numbers, labels, logos, watermarks or extra decorative elements anywhere.

CHARACTER DESIGN LOCK
All fifteen depictions show <Subject 1> as the same adult East Asian woman, with the same delicate oval face, facial proportions, soft nose and lips, violet irises and smooth natural skin. Preserve the reference's dark black-purple long hair, neat straight bangs, symmetrical high twin ponytails and EXACTLY TWO ornate gold branching deer-antler hair ornaments, one at each ponytail root. The two ponytails extend clearly PAST THE WAIST TO THE UPPER THIGHS in every full-body view. Preserve their high twin roots, dark black-purple color, layered hair bundles and paired gold ornaments, while ensuring the full long ponytail length remains visible behind the torso. They are long twin ponytails, never shoulder-length or short ponytails.
Keep the exact purple and lavender fantasy outfit from <Picture 1>: the high ornamental purple collar with gold details, bare shoulders, fitted short bodice with the large central gold flower and layered purple petal motif, exposed midriff, decorated upper arms and translucent pale-purple draping sleeves with gold edging, ornate gold waist trim, layered short skirt/skort with purple and lavender panels and delicate gold embroidered borders. The reference's visible lavender fabric remains lavender; do not recolor it black or simplify its layered construction. Keep all flowers, gold edges, collar pieces, waist ornaments, sleeve openings and layer lengths in corresponding positions across views. Retain the reference's white ribbed short socks and purple low-heel Mary Jane shoes with their single instep strap, closed rounded toe, natural thickness and modest heel. Preserve the same footwear geometry in every angle. Do not add weapons, bags, jewelry or additional hair ornaments. Do not remove existing ornaments. No costume redesign, no new colors, no altered age or facial identity.

LEFT TURNAROUND ZONE
Three separate complete figures occupy only the left 60 percent. All stand in the same relaxed neutral stance, arms naturally lowered slightly away from the torso so garment construction is readable. Hands relaxed, legs straight and parallel, feet on the same baseline. FRONT figure directly faces the camera with symmetrical shoulders and hips. SIDE figure is a true orthographic 90-degree profile, showing only the side silhouette rather than a three-quarter body; her head, shoulders, hips and shoes all face the same side. BACK figure is a true orthographic 180-degree rear view, with the face not visible and shoulders, spine, layered back garment and shoe heels facing the camera. Render consistent body height, adult body proportions, scale, costume geometry and hair length across all three. Align the tops of their heads and soles of their feet on exactly common horizontal lines. Include each full silhouette, both ornaments, the ponytail ends, fingers and both shoes, with comfortable white margins. No cropping, no overlapping figures, no seated pose, no crossed legs. Translate hidden back construction conservatively from the visible reference design, with compatible gold trim and layers rather than adding a different costume.

RIGHT DETAIL GRID: THREE COLUMNS BY FOUR ROWS
Order the twelve cells LEFT TO RIGHT within each row, then TOP TO BOTTOM. Each cell contains ONE specific close-up of the SAME <Subject 1>, cropped for that detail only, with the same white studio background and consistent material appearance.
ROW 1: cell 1, straight-on front head portrait with the face, bangs and paired gold ornaments; cell 2, a camera directly ABOVE her crown looking VERTICALLY DOWN at the TOP SURFACE of her head, clear central scalp parting and both high ponytail attachment points; this cell shows the hair crown from overhead, no face, no neckline, no back-of-head rear portrait; cell 3, rear hair close-up showing both ponytails and the back-of-head construction, no face.
ROW 2: cell 4, exact 90-degree side head profile showing nose, lips, ear and hair silhouette; cell 5, very close view of one violet eye and surrounding softly lit skin; cell 6, 45-degree three-quarter face portrait preserving the same face.
ROW 3: cell 7, central chest gold flower, purple petal layers and bodice fabric texture; cell 8, waist fabric construction and gold waist ornaments; cell 9, rear skirt/skort layers, seams, gold embroidery and compatible back garment details.
ROW 4: cell 10, a tight close-up of her BARE KNEE AND CALF, from mid-thigh down to mid-shin, smooth LEG SKIN with gentle studio light falloff, absolutely no head, no eyes, no nose, no lips and no facial skin; cell 11, extreme macro of the violet iris, eyelashes and eyelid detail; cell 12, complete white ribbed short socks and BOTH purple Mary Jane shoes, showing the straps, rounded toes, soles and low heels with no clipped shoe tips.
Maintain exactly 12 cells, not 9, not 15, not 16. No merged cells, unequal cells, extra rows, extra columns, blank cells or repeated full-body people in this right-hand grid. Do not move any of these twelve close-ups to the left turnaround area.

RENDERING
Premium Japanese 3D game character CG, a production-quality character artist presentation. Fine physically based materials and believable geometry, soft evenly distributed neutral white studio illumination, delicate natural skin texture and subsurface light response, clear violet iris structure, separated high-quality hair strands and layered hair bundles, detailed woven fabric and gold embroidery, accurate translucent purple sleeve fabric, polished gold metal with restrained realistic reflections. Clean sharp edges and subtle local form shading; no harsh cast shadows, dramatic color cast, photographic outdoor backdrop, painterly brushwork or flat anime line art. Keep consistent camera scale for full-body views, consistent material colors in close-ups and impeccable limb anatomy. High detail across the entire board, no motion blur or depth-of-field blur obscuring design details. One complete still reference board.

FINAL PANEL CONTENT CHECK: The bottom-left cell of the right-hand grid MUST be a knee/calf LEG close-up. Only bottom-middle is an eye macro and only bottom-right is shoes. The upper-middle cell MUST be a straight-down overhead crown shot, visibly different from the upper-right rear-hair shot. Third-row-right MUST match the BACK figure's rear skirt embroidery. These are different camera angles and different anatomical regions, not interchangeable face crops. Retain the exact 3 by 4 detail grid and all three full-body figures.
